title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'contrées', a combinatorial and order-theoretic model of tame (PL or semi-algebraic-like) topology. A contrée has cells, and 'figures' are certain finite sets of cells. Two relations are used: subdivision (F' ≃_s F) and inclusion of sub-figures (G ⊂ F). From these one defines refinement: Φ refines F (Φ ≪ F) iff Φ is a sub-figure of some subdivision of F. For a cell X, X ≪ G means X refines G.

Previous page (Proposition): let F be a figure, G ⊂ F a sub-figure, F' a refinement of F, and G' = {X ∈ F' | X ≪ G}. Then G' is a sub-figure of F' that refines G, and it is the largest such sub-figure. Proof: choose a subdivision \bar F' of F containing F'. The subdivision \bar G' of G induced by \bar F' consists of the cells of \bar F' refining G. Then G' = F' ∩ \bar G' is a sub-figure of \bar G', so G' refines G.

This page (Corollary): in the poset of figures ordered by refinement, G' = inf(F', G). That is, any figure Φ refining both F' and G refines G'.

Proof (two diagrams of subdivisions and inclusions):
1. F' ⊂ \bar F, where \bar F is a subdivision of F.
2. Φ ⊂ \bar F', where \bar F' is a subdivision of F'.
3. Extend \bar F' to a subdivision \tilde F of \bar F (hence of F) that induces \bar F' on F'. So \bar F' ⊂ \tilde F ≃ \bar F ≃ F.
4. Let \tilde G be the subdivision of G induced by \tilde F, i.e. the cells of \tilde F refining G.
5. Take X ∈ Φ. Then X ∈ \bar F' ⊂ \tilde F, and X refines G because Φ refines G. Hence X ∈ \tilde G.
6. So X ∈ \bar F' ∩ \tilde G, which is \bar G', the subdivision of G' induced by \bar F'.
7. Therefore Φ ⊂ \bar G' ≃ G', i.e. Φ refines G'. 'qed, ouf!'

Grothendieck remarks this was laborious, apparently noting that it amounts to (or replaces) an axiom 'Cont 8'. On the next page (13 June) he decides to change viewpoint again: the 'quatrième mouture' takes the set of figures with two order relations, ≤ (inclusion) and ≼ (subdivision), as primitive. This lemma, painfully derived here from cell-level axioms, is the kind of order-theoretic fact that motivates that switch.
errors: No mathematical error found. The proof silently uses several axioms. (i) Transitivity of refinement, which needs that a subdivision of a sub-figure extends to a subdivision of the ambient figure (step from \bar F' ⊂ F' to \tilde F). (ii) For a subdivision \tilde F of F and a sub-figure G, the cells of \tilde F refining G form a subdivision of G (the induced subdivision). (iii) Compatibility of induced subdivisions: \bar F' ∩ \tilde G equals the subdivision of G' induced by \bar F'. Point (iii) is asserted ('= \bar G'') without comment. It follows from the description of induced subdivisions as 'cells refining the sub-figure', but strictly needs that refining G' is the same as lying in \bar F' and refining G.
The first diagram is crossed out, apparently a false start using F instead of F'.

ideas.what: Refinement preorder on figures: Φ ≪ F iff Φ is a sub-figure of a subdivision of F. It is built from two primitive relations, inclusion and subdivision.
ideas.modern_name: Refinement order on polyhedral or cell complexes; poset of stratifications/subdivisions in tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Hudson); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: Only as a programme (tame topology) in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'contrée' axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Meet in the refinement order: for a sub-figure G of F and a refinement F' of F, the cells of F' refining G give inf(F', G).
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a refinement to a subcomplex as a meet/greatest lower bound

ideas.what: Recasting the theory as a set with two order relations (≤ inclusion, ≼ subdivision): the 'contrée, quatrième mouture' of the next page, motivated by such lemmas.
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic/lattice axiomatization of tame spaces (cf. posets of subdivisions)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine lemma in an unpublished axiomatic development (contrées). The mathematics is standard PL folklore. The only historical interest is seeing why Grothendieck switched to a bi-ordered-set axiomatics on the next page, and that interest belongs to the larger manuscript, not this page.
transcription_corrections: 'On utilise que F ⊂ \bar F, où F''[?] sous-ensemble de F' should read 'On utilise que F' ⊂ \bar F, où \bar F subd. de F'. The bar is over F, and it is a subdivision, not a subset.
'où \bar F' sous-ens. de F'' should read 'où \bar F' subd. de F''.
'Mais \bar F' est induite par une sous-ens. \tilde F de F' should read '... induite par une subd. \tilde F de F'. Likewise '\tilde G, subd. de G induite par la subd. \tilde F de F'.
'(C'était quand même coton[?])': the image reads 'C'était quand même Cont 8', referring to an axiom numbered Cont 8 (the next page lists Cont 1–7).
'Φ ⊂⊂ G'' in parentheses is better read as 'disons Φ ≪ G''.
The parenthetical '(C G resp. et courage...)' is illegible; it should not be read as 'courage'.
